title: Seeing the small
hookLine: seeing the small is clarity; keeping soft is strength (Tao Te Ching 52)

lines: A CHIP THE SIZE OF A LENTIL.
cards: A pebble ticks off the windshield on the highway. Later, at a gas station, there's a chip the size of a lentil, low on the passenger side. Easy to miss.
Left alone through a few hot days and cold nights, a chip like that can creep into a crack across the whole glass. Caught small, it's a quick repair. Caught late, it's a new windshield.
Chapter fifty-two of the Tao Te Ching has a line for the person who notices the chip, and it calls that noticing a kind of clear sight.

teach.h: KNOW THE MOTHER, KNOW THE CHILDREN.
teach.b: First, the frame. The world had a beginning, the chapter says, and that beginning is like a mother. Know the mother, and you can know her children, the many things of the world.
Know the children, and then hold on to the mother. It wants both: attention to things, and a steady hold on their source. Second, the doors.
Keep the mouth shut, close the gates, and life goes on without exhausting toil. Fling them open, chase every affair, and there's no rescue.
It's an old picture of a life with fewer inputs: less leaking out, less pouring in. Third, today's line.
In James Legge's translation: "The perception of what is small is (the secret of) clear-sightedness; the guarding of what is soft and tender is (the secret of) strength."
The parentheses are Legge's own, filling out the short Chinese. Notice the pairing.

teach.h: CLEAR SIGHT IS CATCHING THE SMALL.
teach.b: Clear sight doesn't come from staring at the big picture; it comes from catching the small. And strength doesn't come from hardening; it comes from guarding what's soft.

teach.h: THE PERCEPTION OF WHAT IS SMALL.
teach.b: The small is often where they start. The friend's texts that have gotten a little shorter. The first sharp word in a meeting.
A tiredness that has hung around for a second week. None of it is dramatic. That's the point.
By the time something is big, it's no longer a matter of seeing. It's a matter of repair.

how: Readers of the Tao Te Ching often treat chapter fifty-two as a teaching about attention: noticing small beginnings, guarding what is gentle, and keeping hold of the source of things.

o: staring at details and missing the big picture
catching things early, while they're still small
looking down on people who seem unimportant

s: chapter fifty-two says clear sight comes from seeing the big picture
it says the perception of what is small is the secret of clear-sightedness.
the chapter links strength to guarding what is soft and tender
not to hardening, but to guarding the soft.
the chapter asks for knowing the children and holding the mother
know the many things, it says, and keep hold of their source.

games.q: you spot a chip the size of a lentil in your windshield. what does chapter fifty-two's line point toward?
o: wait until it's big enough to matter.
games.why: the chapter says perceiving what is small is the secret of clear sight; small is where things begin, and where they're easiest to tend.

practice: Let your eyes rest on one ordinary object near you, a mug, a leaf, the edge of a table, the back of your hand, and look at it as if you'd be asked to describe it later: the texture, the small mark you never saw, the way the light sits on one side.
When your mind drifts to something bigger, come back to the small thing, gently. If you'd rather close your eyes, do the same with one small sound.

wordCard.voice: Seeing the small. Chapter fifty-two says that perceiving what is small is the secret of clear sight, and guarding what is soft is the secret of strength. Today's word.
